CHN.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Stay inside the May 19 framework and keep working-level talks open for agriculture and energy purchases we already need, while refusing any locked $200 billion figure or structural retreat on industrial policy. Condition further purchase specificity on a formal U.S. hold of the Section 301 list and a durable ZTE remedy, not only Mnuchin’s verbal “on hold.” Do not add tariffs or broaden retaliation while Ross is coming to Beijing; that would hand Washington hawks a reason to implement the $50 billion list.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: Threat is real but not yet high. The 16 April Commerce denial order showed the United States can halt a major Chinese tech firm by cutting component access; ZTE stopped major operations and ~75,000 jobs were at risk. The 3 April Section 301 list (~$50B, ~1,300 lines) aims at aerospace, ICT, robotics and machinery—exactly the upgrade sectors. Those duties are not in force, but the comment window is still open and the joint statement is silent on cancelling them. Macros do not show a bite yet: industrial production ~6.8% YoY in May, reserves still ~$3.13T, CPI soft, merchandise exports still expanding, and CNY around 6.39 rather than in a run. That sits between neutral and the +0.5 “major export sectors hit / firm-level targeting” anchor—hence +0.30, not +0.50. Action should stay mild. Escalation would waste Trump’s 13 May instruction to find ZTE a path back and Mnuchin’s 20 May statement that tariffs are on hold while a framework is executed. China already got the purchase language kept vague (no dollar figure after the $200bn leak), which is the right bargain: directional ag/energy buys in exchange for time and a possible ZTE fix. Locking concede_purchases now would pay for a pause hawks (Lighthizer/Navarro camp; comment deadline still live) can reverse without a matching formal 301 withdrawal. Negotiate, do not escalate and do not pre-pay.
key_factors: ZTE denial order demonstrated a U.S. component kill-switch against a major Chinese tech firm
Section 301 $50B list still live and aimed at MIC2025-type sectors, though not yet imposed
19 May joint statement plus Mnuchin 'on hold' created a pause without binding U.S. rollback
China kept purchases directional (ag/energy) and refused a locked $200bn number
Chinese real economy not yet showing trade-war stress (IP, reserves, FX, exports)
Split U.S. team (Mnuchin vs Lighthizer/Navarro) makes a purchase-for-pause path available if we stay at the table

sources_cited.excerpt: US Commerce Department bans ZTE from buying US components (denial order). ZTE faces operational shutdown. Major non-tariff escalation.
USTR publishes proposed Section 301 tariff list: ~1,300 Chinese product lines (~$50B), targeting aerospace, ICT, robotics, machinery and related sectors.
US and China release joint statement after talks: China agrees to "significantly increase" purchases of US goods and services. Mnuchin says trade war is "on hold."
China announces proposed retaliatory tariffs on ~$50B of US goods (including soybeans, automobiles, and aircraft) in response to the Section 301 list.
China industrial production still ~106.8 (same period previous year = 100) as of 2018-05-01; no visible output collapse.
China reserves ex-gold ~$3.13T in May 2018; only about a 1% decline over the window.
CNY at 6.3875 per USD on 2018-05-23, stronger than late-2017 levels; no FX-stress signal.

Joint statement: China will significantly increase purchases; meaningful increases in U.S. agriculture and energy; U.S. will send a team to work out details; IP cooperation and Patent Law amendments; no tariff-cancellation clause.
Mnuchin: "We're putting the trade war on hold... we have agreed to put the tariffs on hold while we try to execute the framework." Beijing did not agree to a $200bn deficit cut.
Statement did not say how much China would buy or whether the U.S. would back down from $50–150B tariffs; public input on the $50B list ends the following week.
Trump tweeted he and Xi are working to give ZTE a way back into business; Commerce exploring alternative remedies; China MFA welcomed the statement.
China pulled back from a reported ~$200bn purchase figure after it leaked; U.S. advisers split between Mnuchin/Kudlow and Lighthizer/Navarro.
